subject: Running 1000 parboot() iterations in parallel takes longer than in serial

messages.author: 4c16debd333db67f
messages.subject: Running 1000 parboot() iterations in parallel takes longer than in serial
parts:
Dear friends,

I'm following the advice here: https://groups.google.com/forum/#!msg/unmarked/txp1UeptjgM/bYHTPiUN55kJ

to run 1000 parboot() simulations in parallel (Amazon EC2, hoping to speed things up by using a 10 cores of a 16-core machine vs. the time required to run these in serial.

For testing purposes I'm using unmarked's Ovenbird data and a gmultmix model from the AHM book. My reproducable code is pasted below, but in summary it's taking ~35 seconds to run 1000 parboot() simulations in serial but ~68 seconds to run 1000 simulations in parallel (100 simulations on 10 cores). So ~2x as long to run them in parallel then in serial, when I expected the parallel option to be faster than the serial one.

I'm using an Amazon EC2 m5.4xlarge instance with 16 vCPUs (stock configuration, no added memory or storage) set up via Louis Aslett's AMI (http://www.louisaslett.com/RStudio_AMI)/

I am obviously doing something wrong and would appreciate any advice from unmarked users experienced in parallel computing.

Many thanks!

Mark B.





> library(parallel)
> library(unmarked)
> 
> 
> fitstats <- function(fm) {
+   observed <- getY(fm@data)
+   expected <- fitted(fm)
+   resids <- residuals(fm)
+   sse <- sum(resids^2)
+   chisq <- sum((observed - expected)^2 / expected)
+   freeTuke <- sum((sqrt(observed) - sqrt(expected))^2)
+   out <- c(SSE=sse, Chisq=chisq, freemanTukey=freeTuke)
+   return(out)
+ }
> 
> # MODEL
> ovenFrame <- unmarkedFrameGMM(ovendata.list$data,
+                               siteCovs=as.data.frame(scale(ovendata.list$covariates[,-1])),
+                               numPrimary=1,type = "removal")
> mod <- gmultmix(~trba, ~1, ~1, data = ovenFrame)
> 
> # SERIAL
> start_time <- Sys.time()
> vals <- parboot(mod, fitstats, nsim=1000) 
> end_time <- Sys.time();total_time<-end_time-start_time; total_time #35 seconds for N=1000 simulations
Time difference of 35.16413 secs
> 
> # PARALLEL
> detectCores()
[1] 16
> cl <- makeCluster(getOption("cl.cores", 10)) #specify cores
> clusterExport(cl, c("mod","fitstats"))
> clusterSetRNGStream(cl, 123) 
> start_time <- Sys.time()
> valp <- clusterEvalQ(cl, { 
+   library(unmarked) 
+   parboot(mod, fitstats, nsim=100) })
> end_time <- Sys.time();total_time<-end_time-start_time; total_time #1.14 minutes for N=10*100=1000 simulations
Time difference of 1.141624 mins
> stopCluster(cl)

messages.author: 4f80e1927b0757cb
messages.subject: Re: Running 1000 parboot() iterations in parallel takes longer than in serial
parts:
Hi Mark,

Assuming you are using a recent version of unmarked, parboot already runs simulations in parallel by default when nsim > 100 (as it is in your case, see ?parboot). On your system, it will do so using 15 of the 16 cores with each running one simulation at time until all 1000 are done. If you want to make sure it is doing so you could run 'top' or similar in a terminal on the AWS instance while it runs and make sure it spawns 15 R processes.

In your second example you are doing batches of 100 simulations at a time on only 10 cores, with the extra overhead of loading the library and running the setup code in parboot() in every core. I'm guessing a combination of the lower number of cores and the extra overhead leads to the extra runtime you are seeing.

Ken

messages.author: 4c16debd333db67f
messages.subject: Re: Running 1000 parboot() iterations in parallel takes longer than in serial
parts:
Hi Ken,

Clearly it's been some time since I've checked out ?parboot. :) That's great news that parboot() now runs in parallel by default when nsim > 100 and your logic below for why my (apparently) serial (but actually parallel) run took less time than my parallel one makes good sense. I'll run a few simulations on single core vs. multi-core machines to confirm.

Thanks again,

Mark
